**Unstructured assessment**  
All done from the “Localization” tab. All z-stacks are being held in memory. Toggling visibility or switching features (double click top right view on feature) increasingly add to memory usage. This is peculiar, since no new data should be created. The first memory optimization should lie in the fact that switching features should actually free up memory, since the inactive features’ z-stacks should be unloaded from memory. Not sure how to do it precisely. Reload from disk after switching features?  
Furthermore, deleting z-stacks does not directly free up memory, but that can have to do with how python keeps unallocated memory reserved (not sure how this works). Deleted (via the cross icon button in the GUI) z-stacks also come back after certain actions: if you had 2 z-stacks for a feature, and delete them (list is empty as it should), then click on bottom left view (Live 1\) and then click on top right view again the deleted ones come back. Not sure how to fix it, should we bookkeep the deletion of these streams from the GUI?  Or just delete the files from the disk as well? For this test I have a folder called /home/tim/Pictures/mem-test. There is a features.json file.
